Coverage gaps: difficulty-aware flagging of underperforming detectors

Source: R/04-benchmark.R
fx_coverage_gaps.Rd

The machine-readable companion to the coverage notes in DEVELOPMENT-STATUS.md (§6.5). Rather than a single flat accuracy gate – which conflates intrinsic difficulty, thin support, and a genuine detector bug – each gold variant is judged on up to four signals and sorted into one of two action buckets, so every flag names its own remedy:

Usage

fx_coverage_gaps(
  res,
  baseline = NULL,
  stress = NULL,
  min_support = 5L,
  target = .FX_COVERAGE_TARGETS,
  baseline_margin = 0,
  stress_drop_max = 0.25,
  conf = 0.95,
  ontology = fx_ontology(),
  include_absent = TRUE
)

Arguments

res

Output of fx_benchmark() (the learned run).

baseline

Optional output of fx_benchmark() run with router = "signature", for the baseline-relative signal. NULL skips it.

stress

Optional output of fx_stress_grid(), for the stress-delta signal. NULL skips it.

min_support

Variants with fewer than this many cases are "needs-cases".

target

A value-accuracy target: either a single number applied to every variant, or a vector named by match_kind (default .FX_COVERAGE_TARGETS: genome/lexicon/mask+lexicon 0.95, mask 0.85, shape/none NA = excluded).

baseline_margin

Flag "needs-detector-work" when baseline_delta is below -baseline_margin (default 0, i.e. any underperformance).

stress_drop_max

Flag "needs-detector-work" when stress_drop is at or above this (default 0.25).

conf

Confidence level for the Wilson interval.

ontology

Ontology table providing the variant_id -> match_kind map (default fx_ontology()).

include_absent

If TRUE (the default), also emit a "needs-cases" row with support = 0 for every live ontology variant that never appears in res — the corpus blind spots the per-case signals cannot see, since they only rank variants that were actually banked. Requires an ontology.

Value

A data frame per gold variant: match_kind, support, acc_type, acc_headline, target, wilson_upper, baseline_acc, baseline_delta, stress_drop, the dominant wrong prediction (top_wrong), and bucket ("needs-detector-work" / "needs-cases" / "excluded" / "ok"), ordered worst first. With include_absent, variants absent from the corpus appear as support == 0 rows in the "needs-cases" bucket.

Details

  1. Per-match_kind target. Achievable precision depends on mechanism: genome / lexicon / mask+lexicon types can reach ~0.95, mask is looser, and header-gated shape / none types are excluded from value accuracy entirely (never scored 0). The target is set by match_kind (joined from ontology); override via target.

  2. Baseline-relative. With baseline (a fx_benchmark(router = "signature") run), baseline_delta is learned minus signature accuracy. A type hard for everyone is difficulty, not a bug; a type where the learned router loses to the model-free floor is a real regression.

  3. Stress-delta. With stress (a fx_stress_grid() grid), stress_drop is the clean type-accuracy minus the mean over applicable perturbed rows. Brittleness to a space or stray case is a detector bug regardless of absolute accuracy.

  4. Support-aware confidence. A Wilson interval on the accuracy estimate; the accuracy test fires only when its upper bound is below target, so thin-support types are not flagged on noise.

Buckets: "needs-cases" (thin support -> bank/generate data), and "needs-detector-work" (adequate support but accuracy upper-bounded below target, or losing to the signature baseline, or stress-brittle -> fix the predicate/recipe). Header-gated types with adequate support are "excluded"; everything else is "ok".

See also

fx_benchmark(), fx_stress_grid(), fx_benchmark_confusion()
